import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 166

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [AKS80] Ajtai, M., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., A note on Ramsey numbers. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos166

/--
Prove that
$$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^{O(1)}}.$$

This is true, and was proved by Mattheus and Verstraëte [MaVe23], who showed that
$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^4}$.
This problem is #5 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_166 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
        (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 4 k : ℝ) ≥
          C * (k : ℝ) ^ 3 / (Real.log k) ^ c := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos166

findings.description: The bibliography entry [MaVe23], on lines 27–28, gives the page range 941–965. The published article occupies pages 919–941. This is only a reference error; the mathematical statement and the documented exponent-4 bound are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher's page, https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2024/199-2/p08, identifies Mattheus–Verstraëte's “The asymptotics of r(4,t)” as “Pages 919-941 from Volume 199 (2024), Issue 2,” DOI 10.4007/annals.2024.199.2.8.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `941-965` with `919-941` in the [MaVe23] bibliography entry.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a positive real exponent, a positive multiplicative constant C, and a non-strict eventual inequality. The original UCSD/Chung–Graham formulation asks for some c such that r(4,n) > n³/(log n)^c for all sufficiently large n, without an explicit multiplicative constant or positivity condition on c.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: From the Lean bound, increase the exponent to c+1. Eventually log k > 1/C, so k³/(log k)^(c+1) < C·k³/(log k)^c ≤ R(4,k). Conversely, the original strict bound yields the Lean bound with C=1; replacing its exponent by max(c,1) ensures positivity without strengthening the eventual bound. A bounded O(1) exponent can likewise be replaced by a fixed positive upper bound. These equivalences were proved for arbitrary functions ℕ → ℝ in the scratch file, independently of the reviewed theorem.

sources_consulted: Mattheus–Verstraëte, The asymptotics of r(4,t), arXiv:2306.04007v5: LaTeX source, introduction, Theorem 1 and its proof, and concluding remarks (https://arxiv.org/e-print/2306.04007v5).
Chung–Graham, Erdős on Graphs, Chapter 2, §2.3.3, p. 12, equation (2.12): https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/epbk/ramsey.pdf
F. R. K. Chung, Open problems of Paul Erdős in graph theory, Ramsey theory section, Problem (6): https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/ep.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization or stale status was found. The sole theorem faithfully states the original conjecture, and Mattheus–Verstraëte's Theorem 1 supplies exponent 4, confirming `answer(True)` and `research solved`. Inspected the Ramsey, graph-copy, complement, natural-infimum, logarithm, real-power, filter, and answer definitions. Lean checks established the clique/independent-set interpretations, R(4,0)=0, R(4,1)=1, R(4,2)=4, positivity of the bound for k≥2, and the stated reformulation equivalences. All experiments compiled successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the reviewed file was not modified. Access limitation: the live erdosproblems.com page and full texts of Sp77/AKS80 were blocked. The original problem was instead checked directly in the UCSD collection and Chung–Graham book, and the solution in MaVe23's LaTeX source. The older papers' bounds were checked through the source literature's summaries; they have no separate declarations in this file.
